title: what tantra actually is
tomorrow: the goddess has heard every answer. what does she still want?

segments.voice: Yesterday, what tantra actually is in a householder's day: every act offered, the house as the place of practice. Today, the last stop in this run of Tantras, and an odd first step.

Before a free throw, some players run the same small ritual: touch the chest, the shorts, the ball, always in order. Odd, until you see how steady it makes them. Here's an older version that's odder still. A worshipper sits before the goddess's image, and before a single flower is offered, before the lamp is lit, they touch their own body, place by place, saying a sacred syllable at each. Why would worship start with your own body?
screen: `TOUCH, TOUCH, BALL.` → `BEFORE THE FLOWER, THE BODY.` → `WHY START WITH YOURSELF?`

segments.voice: The rite is called nyasa, placing. In the tantric worship the Mahanirvana Tantra lays out, the worshipper places the syllables of a mantra on the body, touching each place as the syllable is said. Only then does the outward worship begin. Why start there? Because in this way of thinking, the body isn't an obstacle to get past. It's the first place the divine is invited to live. The worshipper isn't a stained thing creeping toward something pure. They're made ready, made fit, before they offer anything at all. Some people carry a different picture of religion and the body, where the flesh is the problem. Here the flesh is part of the altar. And this is where the run arrives. What tantra actually is, as these lessons have read it: a seed syllable and a diagram, the deity in sound and shape. Shiva and Shakti, never apart. A reputation, answered by its own books. A temple's day, kept in order. A teaching given for a hurried age, walked by a householder at home. And a worship that begins by touching the body with sacred sound. Not a secret thrill. A practice, done with care, with the whole person in it.
screen: `NYASA: PLACING SOUND ON THE BODY.` · `ONLY THEN, THE OUTWARD WORSHIP.` · `THE BODY: PART OF THE ALTAR.` · `THE RUN, GATHERED.` · then, large: `THE WHOLE PERSON IN IT.`

segments.voice: Nyasa itself is usually given by a teacher, so try only its spirit. Rest one hand lightly over your heart for a few breaths, then on the crown of your head, then back in your lap. Let each place be noticed, as if it were being made ready.
What tantra actually is: here, nyasa, placing sacred sound on the body before any outward worship begins.
Keep this one: what tantra actually is, a worship where the body is part of the altar. See you tomorrow.
